# Kition kit rules (read first)

This repository is Kition's `kit.design` kit. These rules come first; the engine rules below still
apply to the engine.

- The kit draws **its own editor**: `web/` is a React app on `@kition/sdk/editor` (kition-sdk's
  shared kit UI library) with the upstream editor's toolbar, Layers and Assets panel, canvas, and
  the Design, Prototype, and Dev panels. A host (Kition, or `web/dev.html` for development) shows
  it in an iframe and talks to it over the Kit UI protocol (`kition-kit-ui/1`, kition-sdk
  `docs/platform/reference/ui-protocol.md`). Style it only with the host's theme tokens, Kition Tessera
  (`@kition/tessera/ui`), and kit-editor components. Labels and command titles are the upstream
  editor's English text, translated by its own upstream catalogs in `web/src/i18n/upstream/` and,
  where those lack a label, by `PHRASES` in `web/src/strings.ts`. Files go only through the host.
- `bindings/wasm` compiles the engine to WebAssembly on the `KitionAI/kition-sdk` crate;
  the editor runs it in a Web Worker. The contract and the Kition platform rules live in kition-sdk
  (`docs/platform/kits/engine.md`, `docs/platform/reference/ui-protocol.md`), the agent protocol
  in KHP (`github.com/kitharness/kitharness`); change them there, never here. `kition-design-kit` must keep
  passing `kition_kit::testing::check_contract`, and `kit.json` must pass kition-sdk's
  `tools/check-manifest.mjs`.
- Tools run in the engine (`KitTools`): pointer, key, and text events in; requests, overlays, and
  a cursor out. Never draw editor chrome into the rendered pixels.
- `bindings/headless` (`kition-design`) serves the same document over the Kit Protocol for Kition's
  agent. It never shows a window.
- The whole repository is licensed under Apache-2.0 ([LICENSE](../LICENSE)); third-party notices are
  listed in `NOTICE`. Upstream is credited only in NOTICE; never write upstream names anywhere
  else.
- CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` calls Kition's reusable kit CI (`kit-ci.yml`), which runs the
  full checks and tests on GitHub, and the Package workflow (`.github/workflows/package.yml`)
  builds the kit package with Kition's reusable `kit-package.yml`. Do not add other workflows,
  and do not start the Package workflow: releasing is the owner's step.

# Kition Design — instructions for agents

Kition Design is the open-source, Rust-native interface design engine behind Kition's Design kit:
frames, auto layout, components and variants, vector networks, styles and variables, prototypes,
and inspection. It is built to WebAssembly for Kition's in-page editor and served headless for
Kition's agent. Siblings:
`../kition-vector`, `../kition-photo`, `../kition-layout`; same conventions.

Kition reads and writes native `.kdesign` files: the design's content (its replica's content,
`kdm/content.json`, and the images it uses), never its history, which is the
replica the host stores (`docs/features/kdm.md` section 3). `.fig` files and the
public REST API file JSON open as imports (best effort).

## Start every session here

1. Read every known shortfall in [`docs/gaps.md`](../docs/gaps.md) and the editor's parity list in
   [`docs/parity/ui-parity.md`](../docs/parity/ui-parity.md). Unless the user gives you a task, pick work from them.
2. Orient → plan → implement + test → verify (screenshot) → record (docs) → commit.

`plan/` is gitignored (local only).

## Non-negotiables

### Clean-room

- Behaviour comes from public documentation and black-box observation of the running incumbent
  app with synthetic documents only. Never read, disassemble or copy anything inside the
  incumbent's application bundle, web bundle or network traffic (names and public listings only).
- Never copy GPL/AGPL code.
- Reference screenshots of the incumbent stay local under the gitignored `plan/` and are never
  committed, published or used as assets.

### Assets: no third-party product iconography or images, ever

- Never add, copy, trace, redraw from, embed or ship any icon, image, illustration, cursor, logo,
  template, UI kit, preset library, font file or screenshot from Figma, Adobe, or any other
  product, or from any source whose license does not allow it. This includes lookalike redraws.
- Every image, icon, font or other asset is original work (Apache-2.0), OSI open source, public
  domain / CC0, or Creative Commons with redistribution allowed, and has a row in
  [`docs/attribution.md`](../docs/attribution.md).
- The editor's icons are original drawings ported from the upstream editor's code-drawn icon set.
  New icons are new drawings, designed from scratch.
- Fonts live in [KitionAI/kition-fonts](https://github.com/KitionAI/kition-fonts), never in this
  repository. The engine uses it only through the optional `KITION_FONTS_DIR` build input
  (`.cargo/config.toml` points it at `../kition-fonts`). Everything must build, test and run
  without it. No Noto CJK or Source Han: Chinese uses Droid Sans Fallback through `addFont`.
- Demo and test content is synthetic or public domain; never personal photos or data.

### Never crash

- No `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!`, `unimplemented!` in shipped code
  (workspace clippy lints deny them; tests may use them). Return `Result`/`Option`; use `.get()`
  for data-derived indexes; slice strings only at char boundaries; check floats are finite; cap
  sizes. A panic kills the editor's worker.
- `kition_design_engine::guard` turns a panicking command into `EngineError::Internal` and rolls the
  document back. It is a safety net, not a substitute for `Result`.
- `unsafe_code = "forbid"` workspace-wide.
- Every crash fix comes with a regression test. The engine has a junk-parameter sweep over every
  command (`crates/engine/engine/src/tests.rs`): extend fuzz and sweep tests when you add
  parsers or commands.

### Architecture

- **Everything is a command.** User-visible behaviour is a command in
  `crates/engine/engine/src/cmd/*` (`spec!(id, label, params doc, undoable, run)`) plus tests.
  The editor, the agent, and the headless kit dispatch the same command ids.
- **Programmatic calls never open dialogs.** Commands only *request* UI (`Session::request_ui`);
  the editor shows the dialog.
- **Layering** is enforced by `cargo xtask layers`: geom/color (L0) → doc (L1) →
  layout/text/pathops/plugin/collab (L2) → render/format (L3) → svg/pdf (L4) → engine (L5) →
  bindings (L6).
- **The editor is thin**: panels read engine state (`inspect`, queries) and act through engine
  commands. Colours come from the host's theme tokens.
- **Time goes through `chrono`.** Never hand-roll calendar conversion.
- **Never break wasm** (`cargo xtask wasm`).

### Checks (local and in CI)

On this machine run only the fast checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
`cargo check -p <touched crates> --all-targets`, the wasm check
(`cargo check -p kition-design-kit --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`), and for editor changes
`cd web && pnpm typecheck`. The full checks run in the kit's CI run on GitHub: clippy,
`cargo test --workspace`, `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests, layers, assets,
wasm) and every `test:*` script of `web/` (`test:flow`, `test:design`, ...). A task is done
when the CI run of HEAD is green and HEAD is on `origin/main`: push, wait and land with
Kition's `scripts/kit-ci.sh` (`push`, `wait`, `failures`, `land`). Commit only the files your
task touched.

## Running and looking at the editor

- There is no desktop app, CLI or control channel in this repository. Drive the engine through
  `Session` in tests, or through the headless kit executable: `cargo run --release -p kition-design`.
- For the in-page editor, run `web/` (`pnpm dev`) and use `web/dev.html` as the host.
- **For UI work, look at the result** (take a screenshot and read the PNG).
- Parallel agents: separate `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per agent, edit only the crates and files you own,
  delete your target directory when done (disk is limited).

[`docs/parity/target-app-parity.md`](../docs/parity/target-app-parity.md) (each feature's status),

files and the generated [`docs/parity/parity-checklist.md`](../docs/parity/parity-checklist.md)
(`cargo xtask parity`). The first three follow `features.yaml`: when a task lands, update its
feature there, then those lists and the affected rows of the other files, in the same commit. Grade by
behaviour, not by whether a menu item exists; err low.
